The `NotesBox` reads `draftNote` and `setDraftNote` from `AppContext`. When `setDraftNote` is called, it updates state in `AppProvider`, which causes all children of `AppProvider` to re-render — including `CardRow` and `ActivityTable`. This is a classic React context re-render problem.

Now I can see the root cause clearly. Let me verify by checking how many rows are in the activity table.

The `TableRow` component is wrapped in `memo()`, but it calls `useAppContext()` inside it to read `theme`. This means every `TableRow` is a consumer of the `AppContext`. When `setDraftNote` is called (on every keystroke in the notes textarea), the `AppContext.Provider` value changes (because a new object `{ user, theme, draftNote, setDraftNote }` is created on each render), which causes all context consumers to re-render — including every `TableRow`.

Even though `TableRow` is wrapped in `memo()`, `memo` only prevents re-renders from parent prop changes. Context changes bypass `memo` entirely. 

So every `TableRow` re-renders on every keystroke, and each render instantiates roughly ten `Intl` formatting and collation objects plus sorts an array, which is costly if there are many rows — I want to check the actual row count to gauge the impact.
